tagline.text: A large waterpark resort on Maribago beach in Mactan

location.label: Location
location.text: M.L. Quezon National Highway, Maribago, Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱10,000~25,000 (per room per night for two, resort package)

children.text: JPark Island Resort and Waterpark is a large resort with a built-in waterpark on Maribago beach, Mactan Island. It is about 15 minutes by car from the airport, which suits short family trips, and hotel guests use the waterpark at no extra charge.

JPark Island Resort and Waterpark is a large resort on the coast of Barangay Maribago in Lapu-Lapu City, on Mactan Island just east of mainland Cebu. According to English Wikipedia and local press (Philstar, SunStar), it held its grand opening in September 2009 under the name Imperial Palace Waterpark Resort and Spa, and it was renamed in June 2014. It was founded by a Korean businessman and is now run by Filipino owners, so it has long been familiar to Korean travelers in the Philippines. The grounds are given as 16.5 hectares by Wikipedia and about 17 hectares by 2019 local press, so roughly 16.5 to 17 hectares.

The defining feature is that a whole waterpark sits inside the resort. Themed pools such as the Wave Pool, Amazon River, Captain Hook's Pool, Toddler's Pool, Island Pool and Beach Pool, plus large water slides, run together like a garden, with a private beach in front. You can walk down from your room in swimwear and play all day, so families with children make up most of the guests. There are also rooms themed on the children's character Pororo and an indoor theme park, which are popular with Korean kids.

The number of rooms differs by source. Wikipedia and 2019 local press give 568 rooms, villas and suites in total (with a 252-room expansion then planned for 820), while some booking sites list more than 800. Either way it is among the largest on Mactan, with Deluxe, Premier, Suite and Pool Villa categories and separate ocean-view versions. About ten restaurants are mentioned, including the Abalone buffet and Korean, Chinese and Mediterranean restaurants, so you can eat well without leaving the resort.

Note that the Mactan shoreline is coral and reef, so if you expect the fine white sand and wide open sea of Boracay you may be disappointed. Think of this as a facility resort where pools, slides, dining and amenities are all in one place rather than a beach destination. Southern attractions such as Oslob and Moalboal, or Cebu City, need a separate car, so it works best to plan some days of resting at the resort and other days for excursions.

Hotel guests use the waterpark pools and slides at no extra charge. The wave pool, the Amazon River and the children's pools are in separate zones, so children of different ages each have somewhere to play. Slides may have height limits, so check the on-site notices.
Several tall slides are the resort's signature, and Wikipedia lists three. Queues are shortest right after opening and toward sunset, and waits can be long at midday and on weekends.

A beach for guests lies in front of the resort, and you can try kayaks, stand-up paddleboards and water bikes. Some equipment may cost extra. The water gets shallow at certain tides, so plan on splashing around rather than deep-water swimming. Bring beach shoes for safety.

blocks.title: Pororo rooms and indoor theme park

children.text: There are suites themed on the children's character Pororo and an indoor theme park inside the resort, handy for spending time with kids on a rainy day. Opening hours and entry conditions are best confirmed with the resort before you go.
Besides swimming, there are play facilities such as mini golf, go-karts, giant chess and electric cars. Some cost extra. Adults can relax at the spa and fitness center.

There are several restaurants, including the Abalone international buffet, seafood and Mediterranean, Chinese and Korean. Breakfast buffet is usually included in the room rate. A Korean restaurant is a relief when kids or parents struggle with local food.
It is about 15 minutes by car from Mactan-Cebu International Airport. Late arrivals and early-morning departures are not a burden. Many room packages include airport pickup, so check when you book.

After check-in, play in the wave pool and children's pool. Late afternoon has gentler sun and shorter slide queues.
Have dinner at an in-resort restaurant such as Abalone. Restaurants get crowded at New Year and in peak season, so eat earlier.
After the breakfast buffet, stroll the private beach and try water sports.

On days with an early flight, set your airport pickup time in advance and pack most of your bags the night before so the morning goes smoothly. With children, keep the last morning's swim light.

The resort is on M.L. Quezon National Highway, so jeepneys and taxis also reach it.
Because the waterpark is the main draw, the dry season with little rain and many clear days is best. Cebu's dry season generally runs from November to May.
December and January are holiday periods with higher room rates, and some packages require a gala dinner over New Year. March to May is hot and humid, but that is actually good for swimming.

Rooms are divided into Deluxe, Premier, Suite, Pool Villa and Pororo Suite, and prices vary with an ocean view. Groups and families with many children will find larger rooms or villas more comfortable. Standard check-in is
and check-out is
, and an early arrival or late departure may incur an extra charge.

Breakfast buffet is often included in the room rate, and for dinner you choose between a buffet and a la carte. Food inside the resort costs more than outside, so if the prices bother you, you can eat once at a nearby Mactan restaurant area. There is a Korean restaurant, so Korean guests can eat comfortably.

On family trips, your room location strongly affects satisfaction. The resort is large and the walk from the room to the waterpark can differ, so ask for a wing close to the pools when you book. The request is not guaranteed, but repeating it at check-in helps. If your child is small, check the bed setup for each room type and the extra bed cost in advance. There is a condition under which children aged 12 and under stay free using existing bedding, but the guidance at the time of booking takes priority for the headcount rules.

Check the latest rates through a travel agency package or an official inquiry rather than comparison sites. The same room can cost different amounts depending on the market (Korean, Japanese or local).
Over New Year, Lunar New Year and Holy Week, minimum-stay and gala dinner conditions may apply, so check when booking.
Bring swimwear, towels and sunscreen. Follow the on-site notices on pool rules and whether personal floats or outside food are allowed.
Slides have height and age limits, so it helps to know your child's height in advance.
The pools are quieter and cooler early in the day. Midday and weekends are crowded.
Prices inside the resort are high, so buy snacks and water at a Mactan supermarket beforehand if needed.
Book southern tours (Oslob, Kawasan Falls) at the resort desk or through an agency, and rest early the night before because they leave at dawn.
If you stay three nights or more, keep one day free for outings. Exploring the markets, restaurants and coastal road on Mactan or taking a nearby island tour makes resort life less monotonous.
Grab and taxis are easy to find in front of the resort, but waits are long in the rain or at rush hour. Leave with time to spare on the day you head to the airport.
Room, day-use and slide operating information changes often with date and season, so confirm directly with the resort before you go.
The Mactan shoreline is shallow and rough with coral and reef, so wear beach shoes and keep an eye on children.
At both the pools and the beach, never leave children alone, and keep a guardian beside them at all times.
The sun is strong and burns easily, so reapply sunscreen often.
Keep valuables in the room safe and do not leave belongings unattended on the beach.
Some leisure facilities may close because of weather or maintenance, so check the latest notices.
